methodology: Read Git-index path inventory and current working bytes from clean wiki checkout, pinned to published revision; no fetch or HTTP probes for individual links.

Resolve inline Markdown/images, explicit reference definitions, HTML href/src, wiki brackets outside fenced code and inline code. Track source-relative intent through full parsed docs/wiki.yaml source/target mapping.

A broken classification means the exact relative path escapes the wiki root or has no tracked file/page-slug target in this published tree. It is not an observed HTTP status. Existing canonical-repository target and exported asset/page are separately reported.
Heading anchors use conservative local GFM-style derivation with duplicate suffixes and explicit HTML ids; no-match is unverified rather than a remotely observed dead anchor.
limitations: No live GitHub rendering or HTTP status probes for each link; absolute external URLs remain unverified unless current canonical index target can be checked.
Inline parser supports the documented common link forms; arbitrary nested Markdown, shortcut reference syntax, autolink text and links inside code examples are not claimed exhaustively parsed.
GitHub wiki root assets may require raw or canonical URLs depending renderer. Local existing path is target existence evidence, not a remote-rendering claim.
Plain-text requirement evidence paths, JSON provenance paths and frame identifiers are inventoried only where actual Markdown/HTML links are present; they are not automatically clickable.
No app source, generated pages, requirements, Git refs, providers, builds, tests or reviewer processes were mutated. Only this separate audit receipt may be created.
overall: Observed export-projection navigation gaps; not a verdict on application behavior or release acceptance
